criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: Critic’s Pick: "The effervescent new musical comedy...is the most charmingly simple show on Broadway right now — a stellar debut for its authors... and the actor Sam Tutty."

criticReviews.author: Caroline Cao
criticReviews.excerpt: "For an optimist, this is a rom-com recipe where familiarity is a feature, not a flaw...is like a warm hot chocolate as respite from the snow."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "This cake isn’t fully baked...For its staging at the Longacre, with an unnecessary intermission that slams the brakes on the action, the director Tim Jackson has slathered the thing in the icing of sentiment and popped his cork"

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "This is a twee, two-character rom-com that could easily be a Hallmark holiday musical... So while this show held me for Act One with its considerable charm, by Act Two, it was hitting turbulence."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "We’ve got a brand new Broadway star. His name is Sam Tutty...he’s hilarious, Shirley Temple endearing and effortlessly magnetic as a puppy-dog Englishman who’s just landed in the five boroughs for the first time."

criticReviews.author: Dalton Ross
criticReviews.excerpt: "Unfortunately, all that momentum is eventually stymied due to the inevitable conflict that by law must arrive between any couple in a romantic comedy. "

criticReviews.author: Dan Rubins
criticReviews.excerpt: "Two Strangers, spanning two days of personal growth in two hours and 20 minutes (including intermission), is both far too long for the audience’s attention and far too short for Dougal and Robin’s transformations."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: "It is an act of prestidigitation: Entertainment and real emotional engagement are pulled out of thin air."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "“Maybe Happy Ending” [is] a ravishing addition to the catalog of Broadway nerdicals. The term is high praise, honoring supersmart, usually small-scale shows — like “Fun Home,” “The Band’s Visit” and “Kimberly Akimbo” — that nevertheless have big emotional impact. This one, directed with breathtaking bravura by Michael Arden, gets bonus points for difficulty, too"

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Maybe Happy Ending [is] an exceptionally well-oiled and visually sublime production... Broadway newcomer Helen J. Shen shines as Claire... Director Michael Arden’s gorgeous staging makes the most of Dane Laffrey’s multilevel sets behind sliding panels and George Reeve’s floor-to-ceiling videos... Maybe Happy Ending has theatrical magic."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Maybe Happy Ending stands out for both its intimacy and its originality. Arden and his actors approach the material with a delicate touch; they trust the romantic comedy to be charming, which it is, and let the wistfulness emerge naturally."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "Michael Arden’s slick production... might feel like 2064 on the surface, but in its nostalgic, rechargeable heart, the show parties like it’s 1999... Shen and Criss are the ones who make it work. Shen especially is a delight to watch, with an open, emotive face full of quicksilver expressions and a tartness that can turn explosive when she needs it to."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "Maybe Happy Ending dazzles with its love story and astounds with its visual accomplishments. There's nothing robotic about this production: it wears its heart on its sleeve and on charm alone, succeeds."

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: "Both Criss and Shen give excellent, very different performances... One of the achievements of the production is the very complete world that director Michael Arden has created. The sleek, futuristic set (by Dane Laffrey) draws on Korean design, provides a clear sense of time and place... “Maybe Happy Ending” is an undeniably moving, well-made, adorable musical, and it is a pleasant surprise to see an audience weep at a show about two robots in love."

criticReviews.author: Rex Reed
criticReviews.excerpt: "I can only tell you how impossible it is to relate the freshness, the joy and the quality that elevate every aspect of this extraordinary work of theatre artistry. While the rapturous music and lyrics by the team of Will Aronson and Hue Park break your heart, the dazzling direction by Michael Arden reaches levels of perfection in staging and the technical marvels in the settings by Dane Laffrey leave you slack-jawed with awe. There is nothing familiar, no “seen it before” feeling to the action sequences that unfold... I love this show and cannot wait to see it again—and often."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "The odd and simple premise of “Maybe Happy Ending” accomplishes something profound, in examining the nature of connection."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "...musical about have-not teenagers in a have-it-all world."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "adaptation of the classic novel rumbles with talent"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "its approach misses the central thrust of Hinton’s story."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Outsiders is taking a real swing"

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “ 'The Outsiders' will hit the bull’s-eye."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "...takes a milder approach, peering under the hood of masculinity"

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: "...has great visual touches but falters when the characters open their mouths"

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "The tender tune, accompanied by an acoustic guitar...it’s a moment of pure catharsis"

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: "CRITIC’S PICK:...easily stands out as one of the rare must-sees in a crowded season."

criticReviews.author: Gillian Russo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Alicia Keys musical is on fire with powerhouse performances"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Hell’s Kitchen is ultimately a celebration of the city—and the people who make it pop."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "worth being wary of any musical that positions itself as a love letter to New York City."

criticReviews.author: Aramide Tinubu
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a sparkling story paying homage to New York"

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s a show that’s true to its city."

criticReviews.author: Dalton Ross
criticReviews.excerpt: "Lively choreography and powerhouse vocal performances...overcome a so-so story."

criticReviews.author: Zachary Stewart
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s not happily ever after, but a promising beginning."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: CRITIC’S PICK: "You have to admire the glee and cheek with which Escola mauls American history, drawing humor from the collision of high importance and low piffle, puncturing one while elevating the other."

criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "the entire ensemble elevates very silly jokes into a work of art that keeps you riveted from start to finish"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "I can’t remember the last time I saw a play that made me laugh, helplessly and loudly, as much as Oh, Mary! did—and my reaction was shared by the rest of the audience"

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “'Oh, Mary!' is directed by Sam Pinkleton at a breakneck speed that both allows room for the best jokes to harvest their share of laughter while never letting even the lesser gags land with a thud."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Oh, Mary! is a deliriously campy take on that well-known House Divided. A couple houses, in fact."

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: "The puns, bits, and gags zip by in quick succession, and the audience laughs nearly the entire 90 minutes. It is unquestionably the funniest, gayest, campiest play Broadway has seen in years."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "Every single one of Escola’s glugs, put-downs, punchlines, glares and loony line deliveries is a scream."

criticReviews.author: Thom Geier
criticReviews.excerpt: "...Oh, Mary! delivers a solid 80 minutes of gut-busting laughs"

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: "The score to this 'Great Gatsby' is missing a vital urgency."

criticReviews.author: Caroline Cao
criticReviews.excerpt: "I felt the warmth in 'The Great Gatsby,' but it was begging to bring on the heat."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "To audiences hungry for glitz this year, The Good 'Gatsby' may be good enough."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "...this Gatsby feels like it belongs on a cruise or in a theme park."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: " ‘Gatsby’ brings back Big Broadway but lacks heart"

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: "...has glamour but little grit"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a grand, crowd-pleasing spectacle"

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a hodgepodge of many other shows that came before it."

criticReviews.author: Jason Zinoman
criticReviews.excerpt: "It wants to make you scream and maybe chuckle to yourself about it, though its most disturbing suggestion is that the descent into conspiratorial thinking might feel a little like falling in love."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Amid crafty scenic metamorphoses, blood, violence, and pyrotechnics, the showâs most special effects are performances by Coon and Smallwood."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "The slipperiness of ostensible skepticism into utter credulity is what makes Bug continue to resonate so powerfully today."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "To really do its work, Bug needs to get under our skin, and here it never quite does. Weâve got to feel not only the ick but the itch."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "Itâs a thriller that turns the screws so unnoticeably you begin squirming before you notice how efficiently the play has gotten, well, under your skin."

criticReviews.author: Aramide Tinubu
criticReviews.excerpt: â 'Bug is as intimate as it is intense...The performances are also outstanding."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "The sensationally unnerving Broadway premiere of 'Bug'... reads like an origin story for our climate of mistrust and isolation."

criticReviews.author: Shania Russell
criticReviews.excerpt: "It's near impossible not to peek through your fingers: Bug is all absorbing."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "In retrospect, Wicked seems an early sign of the cultural clout which is to say buying power of a generation of girls (and now women) whose desire to see, read, and sing along with stories about female empowerment has become a snowballing trend."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "A musical prequel to The Wizard of Oz, that explained how the Wicked Witch of the West got that way, and explored her true relationship to Glinda the Good Witch. A combination of outstanding elements."

criticReviews.author: John Simon
criticReviews.excerpt: "Two of the producers of the musical Wicked bear the name Platt, which (in German) means flat, and one the name Stone, which (in English) means heavy. Why not also one called Long, although it is too much to ask for one called Boring, all of which apply to the show."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "The best moments in 'Wicked' come when the stage is least crowded. I'm done niggling. 'Wicked' is funny and touching and full of beans (not to mention child-friendly). It'll make a great movie one of these days, and it's going to make Kristin Chenoweth a star right this minute. Go."

criticReviews.author: Rex Reed
criticReviews.excerpt: "Nothing in Oz, you see, happened the way Judy Garland thought it did. In 'Wicked', the ruby slippers aren’t even red. So, all ye who enter here, check your cynicism at the door and get in touch with the little kid inside you who’s been begging to get out. Neither of you will want to leave 'Wicked.'"

criticReviews.author: Clive Barnes
criticReviews.excerpt: "What is spectacular about the show is the spectacle. That old Emerald City has never had it so good, with flying monkeys and giant Munchkins with extendable necks. Kids will love it, even if they don’t quite understand it. But this yellow brick road is also paved with oppressive music and banal, if sometimes pretentiously amusing, lyrics and a complex, if foolish, book."

criticReviews.author: Alice King
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Wicked's' at its cleverest with the girl stuff; the streamlining of Maguire’s story – reducing a totalitarian allegory to an animal-rights flap – weakens the narrative logic. Catchy Stephen Schwartz songs compensate for a dreary opening number, but it’s the 'Wicked' witches who really make magic."

criticReviews.author: Barbara Siegel
criticReviews.excerpt: "It's an ambitious musical...There are so many wonderful things in Wicked that to dismiss it as so many critics have done strikes us as perverse...It has a heart, a brain, and the nerve to have opened on Broadway."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt:
CRITIC'S PICK
"Yes, it really is that good...I am loath to tell people to mortgage their houses and lease their children to acquire tickets to a hit Broadway show. But 'Hamilton,' directed by Thomas Kail and starring Mr. Miranda, might just about be worth it — at least to anyone who wants proof that the American musical is not only surviving but also evolving in ways that should allow it to thrive and transmogrify in years to come."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "What is left to say? After every critic in town (including me) praised the Public Theater world premiere to high heaven; and after seeing this language-drunk, rhyme-crazy dynamo a second time, I can only marvel: They used up all the damn words. Wait, here are three stragglers, straight from the heart: I love 'Hamilton.' I love it like I love New York, or Broadway when it gets it right. And this is so right."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "A second look suggests that something even more significant is going on. The breakthrough isn’t so much the incorporation of those contemporary genres; after all, Miranda already did that, throwing in Latin music to boot, in the charming 'In the Heights.' But 'Hamilton' not only incorporates newish-to-Broadway song forms; it requires and advances them, in the process opening up new territory for exploitation. It’s the musical theater, not just American history, that gets refurbished. And perhaps popular music, too. Call it Miranda’s manifest destiny, though one dreads the caravans of poor imitators that will surely trail behind."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Hamilton' is the best and most important Broadway musical of the past decade. Why important? Because it sounds as though it had been written last week instead of a half-century ago...So do whatever you have to do short of grand larceny to score a ticket to 'Hamilton.' It’ll make you want to stand on your seat and yell with delight."

criticReviews.author: Jeremy Gerard
criticReviews.excerpt: "Every great musical improves on second (and third, and fourth) hearing; 'Hamilton' is no exception. Lin-Manuel Miranda’s magnificent adaptation is not, to use that tired cliché, a game-changer. It is, in truth, the quintessence of a Broadway musical destined for the record books...Like 'Rent' 20 years ago and 'A Chorus Line' 40 years so, 'Hamilton' is accessible without pandering and inspirational in sneaky ways that permeate a skeptic’s shell."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "With 'Hamilton,' Broadway is officially the coolest place on the planet. And the smartest. And most exhilarating. Yes, composer, lyricist, author and leading man Lin-Manuel Miranda’s magical musical tour of the life of the '10-dollar Founding Father,' Alexander Hamilton, is that great. It’s even richer and more eloquent since its run earlier this year at the Public Theater."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "This innovative show is shaping up to be just as much of a phenomenon uptown, playing in a Broadway house with four times the seating capacity, and to a more traditional but no less enthusiastic audience. That universal appeal to crossover audiences is one unmistakable sign of a groundbreaking show...Like any true landmark, 'Hamilton' stands up to repeated viewings. After six months, the show’s initial impact hasn’t dulled a bit; in fact, the qualities that made it so extraordinary the first time around are all the more striking."

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: "Having already become a cultural phenomenon in its off-Broadway premiere run earlier this year at the Public Theater, 'Hamilton' — written by and starring Lin-Manuel Miranda, who previously made a name for himself on Broadway with 'In the Heights' — seems a shoo-in for smash hit status and a slew of awards attention...The musical is a triumph."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: "You can only marvel at the exotic procession of animals before you: the giraffes and the elephants and the hippopotamuses and all those birds in balletic flight. These are creatures of air and light and even a touch of divinity. Where are you, really, anyway? Somehow you have fallen into what appears to be a primal paradise. Such is the transporting magic wrought by the opening 10 minutes of ''The Lion King.''"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Taymor populates the stage with an amazing menagerie of beasts; her audacious staging expands a simple cub into the pride of Broadway, not merely a fable of heredity but a celebration of heritage."

criticReviews.author: John Simon
criticReviews.excerpt: "You will be bombarded by some of the most beautiful and spectacular sights theater can offer from before and behind, so eyes in the back of the head will come in handy.

criticReviews.author: Steven Suskin
criticReviews.excerpt: "'The Lion King' was astonishing, in the jaw-dropping manner of speaking. And today, 21 years later, it still is...Taymor, the avant-garde director to whom Disney entrusted the piece, outdid herself...Everything still looks wonderful, and looks practically brand new, too. One of the stunning elements for me, this time through, was the realization of how brilliantly this show moves...The hard-working ensemble is well-drilled and exceptional."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Oxfeld
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s Julie Taymor’s puppetry that continues to astound...The problem is that the rest of the musical is not as good as Taymor’s vision for the animals and their gorgeous ensemble numbers...Now, the beauty is there, but the show feels a bit worn...The few big numbers aside, much of the John-Rice score is middling ’90s pop rock...That said, the performances, even now, are rather lovely...But you’re not here for the performances. You’re here for the puppets. And they’re worth it."

criticReviews.author: Frank Scheck
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Lion King is a spectacular rendition of the animated film, a brilliant theatrical adaptation that stands on its own...Taymor has risen to the challenge, translating the physically complex tale to the stage with an endlessly clever, visually stunning use of masks, puppetry, costumes and scenic effects; the stage show has the delighted audience firmly in its grip."

criticReviews.author: Michael Sommers
criticReviews.excerpt: "A stunning stage event. Combining a graceful horde of actors, singers and dancers with a stylized world of fantastic puppets and theatrical wonderment."

criticReviews.author: Michael Kuchwara
criticReviews.excerpt: "Make no mistake: The Lion King is a rare theater experience. The musical is intelligent spectacle, extravagance with a purpose -- and a heart. From the moment it begins, The Lion King offers astonishing stage magic. Performers walking on giant stilts become giraffes, birds, and a pride of lionesses, dance with a solemn gracefulness that is breathtaking."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: The pulse-racing revival of the musical ''Chicago,'' involves a cast of top-flight artists perfectly mated to their parts and some of the sexiest, most sophisticated dancing seen on Broadway in years...The America portrayed onstage may be a vision of hell, but the way it's being presented flies us right into musical heaven."

criticReviews.author: Howard Kissel
criticReviews.excerpt: "Because the revival of "Chicago" is so wildly entertaining, I'm hesitant to call it important, always an ugly adjective for a reviewer to use...What makes this revival important, is that it reminds us that musicals are about songs and performers, not scenery. When you have material and performances as dynamic as this, you don't need chandeliers."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "If the Kander & Ebb style can be described in one word, it’s showstopper. And though their detractors might argue that the tenacity can be wearying, they’ll find scant support for that position in “Chicago.” Even in a concert staging, the momentum starts high and gets higher."

criticReviews.author: Zachary Stewart
criticReviews.excerpt: “I am typically of the opinion that no show has any business occupying a Broadway house for more than a decade: Theater is ephemeral, and the magic tends to wear off as the years pass and performances become stale. ’Chicago’ makes this a difficult position to maintain. Ten thousand performances later, it's still dazzling.”

criticReviews.author: Andy Propst
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Broadway revival of John Kander and Fred Ebb's Chicago, may be on the verge of celebrating its 15th anniversary, but one could hardly tell the production has recently entered the upper echelon of long-running shows on Broadway. There's a crispness to the entire piece of Chicago, that belies its age."

criticReviews.author: Matthew Murray
criticReviews.excerpt: "Chicago is as good now as it's ever been--a heartening experience, a life-affirming dedication to the magic and art of theatre, and something that absolutely should not be missed. Though all shows must eventually close, the glory and genius of Chicago should be celebrated while it's here, and with any luck, it will still be gracing and energizing Broadway for many years to come."

criticReviews.author: Elyse Sommer
criticReviews.excerpt: "What it's all about: 'murder, greed, corruption, violence, exploitation, adultery and treachery.' Of course what it's also about is sensational dancing, singing, acting...and, fun! No razzle-dazzle mechanical props, just the razzle-dazzle of a company of gifted performers delivering two hours and twenty minutes of show-stopping numbers."

criticReviews.author: Michael Kuchwara
criticReviews.excerpt: "A lot of Broadway musicals don't age very well, but the long-running revival of 'Chicago' seems to have discovered the fountain of youth. The score's catchy melodies are potent, toe-tapping reminders of music from the late 1920s, while the lyrics are snappy, pointed and often very funny."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: CRITICâS PICK "âMoulin Rouge! The Musicalâ Offers a Party, and a Playlist, for the Ages. Forbidden pleasures abound in this spectacular musical, starring a dazzling Karen Olivo as a doomed Parisian chanteuse."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: ââââ "Red alert! Red alert! If you're the kind of person who frets that jukebox musicals are taking over Broadway, prepare to tilt at the windmill that is the gorgeous, gaudy, spectacularly overstuffed 'Moulin Rouge! The Musical.' Directed with opulent showmanship by Alex Timbers, this adaptation of Baz Luhrmann's 2001 movie may be costume jewelry, but its shine is dazzling."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "'Moulin Rouge!' Is Broadwayâs Biggest Karaoke Night. It commits singlemindedly to stuffing as many additional hit tracks as possible."

criticReviews.author: Alexandra Schwartz
criticReviews.excerpt: "A Millennial Reboot of Chekhov, and 'Moulin Rouge!' on Broadway. Halley Feiffer translates 'Three Sisters' into Internet-speak, and Baz Luhrmannâs glitzy movie comes into its own onstage."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "âMoulin Rouge! The Musical!â Review: Pop Opera Excess. A stage adaptation of Baz Luhrmannâs 2001 camp extravaganza is as opulent as it is empty."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "âMoulin Rouge! The Musicalâ Review: All You Need Is Love Songs By The Dozens"

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "Broadwayâs âMoulin Rouge! The Musicalâ is dazzling, decadent live translation of 2001 movie."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "The luscious 2001 movie hit makes it successfully to the stage â elephant and all â in this gorgeously flashy version."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "This latest musical adapted from one of Disney’s popular movies defied my dour expectations...“Aladdin” has an infectious and only mildly syrupy spirit. Not to mention enough baubles, bangles and beading to keep a whole season of “RuPaul’s Drag Race” contestants in runway attire."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Aside from the tonic of Iglehart’s djinn, however, Aladdin is short on magic."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "So why is Aladdin a bit of a chore? Even the best of what the writers offer doesn’t seem to stick very long; if it weren’t for Nicholaw’s merciless flogging, you feel the story would simply evaporate in the desert heat."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "It's not nearly as good as the movie, but it does have a terrific star, super-duper sets and sensational special effects."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show is as colorful as the Crayola 64 box, and as tirelessly energetic as a toddler, but it also feels canned. While burning through wishes, you should ask for the musical to have a lot more heart. The absence is glaring, given that Disney excels at tugging at tickers and then making them melt."

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "This super-costly extravaganza doesn't do justice to the movie, or to the spirit of the late Howard Ashman."

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: "While it doesn't rival the imagination or innovation of "The Lion King,"  the show's ebullient comic spirit should make it a popular hit. It's not the most sophisticated entertainment, but the target demographic won't mind at all."

criticReviews.author: Peter Marks
criticReviews.excerpt: "This version of 'Aladdin' will doubtless keep your kiddies happy; for adults, one would like to press Iglehart in the cause of conjuring a desert kingdom of richer enchantments."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt:
CRITIC'S PICK
“The sumptuous, hypnotic and somewhat hyperactive musical...Chavkin and her creative team have saved ‘Hadestown’ on its way uptown by turning it into something very much warmer...The story is clearer...’Hadestown,' even with the heat turned up, is still a somewhat abstract experience...Mitchell develops her larger themes mostly through metaphor. This can get tiring; even though so much of what happens happens beautifully."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “Mitchell’s fizzy, moody, thrilling new musical....Although the narrative has gained some bulk since 'Hadestown’s' Off Broadway run, it is still wight-thin...Yet somehow that hardly matters: ‘Hadestown’ sweeps you up in its atmospherics and in the intensity of its eco-Marxist vision of solidarity and the liberating potential of art...Most important, it has Mitchell’s score: a joyful combination of folk, pop, Dixieland and blues that will make you want to rehear it as soon as the lights come up.”

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: “’Hadestown’ has arrived...And its current manifestation feels lush, vigorous, and formally exciting, not to mention witchily prescient...As an intricate and gorgeous feat of songwriting, as a vehicle for dynamite performances, as a visionary long-term collaboration and a courageous experiment with form, ‘Hadestown’ is cause for celebration...Mitchell’s lyrics are image-rich and clever, her tunes exhilarating...Page and Gray are the twin sensations of the show.”

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: “Hadestown” isn’t perfect, but it’s so fresh that you’ll gladly look past its forgivable flaws and savor the kaleidoscopic stylistic variety of Ms. Mitchell’s score...Mitchell’s down-home score is the incontestable star of the show...Mitchell’s songs are beautiful but undramatic...Chavkin’s endlessly varied direction and Neumann’s dances help to keep things on the move...Would that ‘Hadestown’ were a bit shorter, too, but there’s no point in fussing over a show as rich as this one.”

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: “The most thrilling new original musical of the season...Carney’s is perhaps the riskiest interpretation...The choice might strike some as mannered, but it worked for me...With an ending as moving as anything on Broadway – and for hades’ sake, don’t leave before the cast finishes its curtain call – ‘Hadestown’ stands alongside Fish’s ‘Oklahoma!’ and Sher’s ‘Mockinbird’ as this Broadway season’s visionary triumvirate, looking to the past and feeling undeniably, stirringly now.”

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: “The thrillingly alarmist new Broadway musical with the score that feels like it comes from somewhere deep in the American gut...An eye-popping, mythological blend of steampunk...’Hadestown’ feels like the most relevant and resistant musical in town, but it never comes off as shrill or moving in some kind of dull lockstep with all the other self-aware plays and musicals lamenting Trump’s America by playing tritely to the choir, critics and all.”

criticReviews.author: Marilyn Stasio
criticReviews.excerpt: "With its earthly delights more or less intact, this perfectly heavenly musical should stick around for a while....Although the production has lost some of the electricity that goes with playing in the round, Chavkin...has done a super job of adapting this pretty thing for a proscenium stage...The world on top looks a bit like New Orleans...But the real action happens in hell, depicted here by the entire company in a rousing number, 'Way Down Hadestown,' that could make the dead dance.”

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: “A seamless theatrical experience, this beguiling, virtually sung-through musical is notable for the expressive beauty of its score, the dark imagination of its stage pictures and the clarity of its storytelling. Performed by a first-rate cast and played with spirited feeling by seven onstage musicians, it arrives on Broadway with a furnace-like blast of creativity...Though it ends on a note of desolate loss, this spellbinding musical sends you out on a high."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Wheeldonâs choreography â performed by Frost along with a superb if amazingly jacked ensemble â remains compelling longer, offering a three-dimensional version of what most of us have seen only from distant arena seats or in dark videos on depthless screens. (The showâs âMichael Jackson movementâ is credited to two additional choreographers, Rich + Tone Talauega.) The stage patterns are far more varied and expressive than in similar musicals, scoring points without words as they deliver the thrills and, following the biomusical road map, pave the way between present and past...In this, âMJâ is trying to have it both ways. It wants to blame everything sad and weird about Jackson on others (especially the press, who are equated with the zombies in âThrillerâ) but credit him alone for his every good deed and success. Acknowledgment of the choreographers and songwriters he collaborated with is mostly saved for the program."

criticReviews.author: Ayanna Prescod
criticReviews.excerpt:
"Paul Tazewellâs magnificent costume design carries the cast through the MJ timeline seamlessly. A killer set by Derek McLane, amplified by gorgeous lighting by Natasha Katz, gives the show a visual beauty that makes it hard to look away.

While Jackson's story is flawed, itâs too complicated for anyone who hasnât danced in his shoes. MJ The Musical, however, is the perfect salutation to the life of an imperfect but gifted icon."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "The dancers and singers of the ensemble, who double as secondary characters, are first-rate, and Wheeldon gives them a lot to do. Most of the songs are performed as rehearsals or flashbacks, which is to say as full-on production numbers. (Tracks from Jacksonâs 1995 album HIStory are cannily placed by Nottage as character moments.) Like Summer and The Cher Show before it, MJ uses three actors to play its central character at different ages. As the 1992 incarnation, Frost carries the bulk of the role, and not only nails Jacksonâs signature sound and movesâyes, of course thereâs a moonwalkâbut also his otherworldly affect: his diffident grandiosity, his mixture of grievance and mischief, his high and breathy way of talking (at once floaty and determined, like Diana Rossâs spoken-word section of âAinât No Mountain High Enoughâ)."

criticReviews.author: Helen Shaw
criticReviews.excerpt: "If there is a scientific experiment to discover whether or not a jukebox musical ruins even our greatest playwrights, this is it. Perhaps it would have been better just to let her go free. MJ wants to be a concert so much â freed from narrative, it could just be bop after banger after blockbuster, the Beatlemania of our time, animated by Myles Frostâs uncanny portrait. Every moment when people are speaking instead of singing feels wrong. As a concert, it could simply elide all those inconvenient and tragic elements of the Michael Jackson legacy. So why isnât it one?"

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Watching MJ, one easily suspects its top-flight creative team was motivated by the same near-maniacal drive. Aside from the pedestrian framing device, MJ pushes hard and unceasingly to move beyond the just-good-enough nostalgia that can turn even second-rate jukebox productions into crowd pleasers. It succeeds: MJ is a wildly entertaining marvel."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "In answer to the question of whether itâs possible to separate the art from the artist, âMJâ performs a slick, crotch-grabbing sidestep. Packed with nearly 40 hits from Michael Jacksonâs irresistible catalogue, the Broadway production from director and choreographer Christopher Wheeldon is not so much a biomusical as a high-shine and surface-skimming rehabilitation tour for its late subject, flattening rather than reckoning with his complex legacy."

criticReviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye
criticReviews.excerpt:
"During a preview I attended, an audience member rose to her feet and waved her hands in the air, as if she had caught the Holy Spirit: an affirmation that to be in Jacksonâs presence â even if only through gifted performers â is to experience a spiritual rapture. 

MJ, like its subject, is captivating and hard to shake. The musical takes audiences through Jacksonâs life and catalog with impressive ease, expertly chronicling major milestones."

criticReviews.author: Peter Marks
criticReviews.excerpt: "That sordid history would not seem to have foretold a jukebox musical devoted to the upside of Jacksonâs genius â and certainly not by artists of the caliber of two-time Pulitzer winner Nottage (âRuined,â âSweatâ) and the celebrated ballet world fixture Wheeldon. The showâs decidedly selective memory may be off-putting to theatergoers appalled by the stories of Jacksonâs alleged misdeeds. Nevertheless, the creative teamâs painstaking work has resulted in a riveting, adrenaline rush of a show, propelled by remarkable dancing and a mesmerizing central performance by Myles Frost as the sleek, soft-spoken pop megastar."

criticReviews.author: Suzy Evans
criticReviews.excerpt:
"The show itself is a retro-mashup with Gabrielle Slade’s bedazzled costumes featuring Reformation-inspired silhouettes; Carrie-Anne Ingrouille’s choreography showcases Tudor-meets-pop moves; and Emma Bailey’s scenery and Tim Deiling’s lighting feels like what a royal ballroom might look like in a techno disco. 

Ultimately, the queens’ own stories of overcoming struggles and the show’s circuitous journey to Broadway are also beacons for the power of positivity, perseverance, and coming together in times of struggle. Just like these six “ex-wives,” we’ve all had it rough for the past year and a half, and the queens are here to bring in a new regime. Long may they reign."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "At heart, Six is a sparkly lark—Hamilton Extra Lite, with the multiculturalism and anachronism and knowing name-dropping but without the plot, emotion and depth...Six is not deep. Six is fun. Let yourself go and enjoy the finery."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Somehow managing to seem loose and improvisational without missing a beat, the cast (backed by a hard-rocking all-female four-piece band called The Ladies in Waiting) is pretty much flawless, one as good as the next and each distinguishing herself when the time comes."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: Best of all, Six is an original musical, with a wildly novel concept, put together by a young creative team, many of them in their twenties. This is how musical theatre moves forward, not by recycling yesterday's hits but by applying fresh thinking and up-to-date wit to a seemingly unlikely subject.

criticReviews.author: Steven Suskin
criticReviews.excerpt: "not what you might call a traditional musical, nor what formerly would have been considered a well-crafted one. But it has mass appeal, immediacy, enthusiasm, and an incredibly high sense of style; and it revels in what used to be called “girl power” but can now more properly be described as simply, or not-so-simply, power."

criticReviews.author: Melissa Rose Bernardo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Six brings together a sextet of badass queens—clad in brilliant chain-trimmed corsets, studded black boots, and spiky crown-like headpieces designed by Gabriella Slade—to compete, American Idol–style, for a somewhat dubious honor: Who took the most crap from that self-serving, Church-splitting, six-times-married monarch?"

criticReviews.author: Joseph Pisano
criticReviews.excerpt: "Indeed, as the queens take their respective turns in the spotlight, spectacle does overwhelm decorum, as the actors stunningly evoke the vocal stylings and stage presences of Beyoncé, Adele, Rihanna, and a few others I probably didn’t catch."

criticReviews.author: Tulis McCall
criticReviews.excerpt: "They have created a generous, funny, provocative show that races by you, grabs your hand and flies up into the stratosphere."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt:
CRITIC'S PICK
"On my fourth visit on a recent night, the show still had me at “Hello,”...I had anticipated a certain falling off of religious fervor: three years is a long time for a peppy musical to stay peppy. But gosh darn it if I didn’t feel born again all over again, ready to spread the word about the faith that this show preaches and, more importantly practices: the holy faith of musical comedy."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "Brimming with cheerful obscenity, sharp satire and catchy tunes, The Book of Mormon is a sick mystic revelation, the most exuberantly entertaining Broadway musical in years."

criticReviews.author: Scott Brown
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Book of Mormon, arriving after months of hype, somehow delivers even more than its ridiculously felicitous advance buzz promised: It’s an often uproarious, spiritually up-tempo satire not just of Mormonism, and not just religion in general, but of (no kidding) Occidental civilization itself."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Oh boy, it's a real winner.The show is blissfully original, irreverent, outspoken and hilarious. And all that's tucked inside good -- no, great -- old-fashioned musical. It's a show where you catch yourself laughing one minute, mouth agape the next, eventually wiping away tears, and, finally, cheering."

criticReviews.author: Steven Suskin
criticReviews.excerpt: "Every song enhances the hilarity, expert staging heightens every gag, and the cast of fresh faces is blissfully good. Broadway hasn’t seen anything like it since Mel Brooks came to town with “The Producers,” only “Mormon” has better songs."
“Money can buy you happiness! If you’re in possession of a ticket, you’ve wisely secured a seat in the premier-class cabin of delirium.”

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: "It’s a fiendishly well-crafted, hilariously smart — or maybe smartly hilarious — song-and-dance extravaganza. The show’s a hoot. The show’s a hit."

criticReviews.author: Lisa Schwarzbaum
criticReviews.excerpt: "An exhilarating Broadway musical at once revolutionary and classic, funny and obscene, uncompromising in production standards and unafraid of just about anything else."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Jukebox musicals may still be bottom feeders, but, as '& Juliet' proves, there are sometimes small treasures to be found in the murk."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "The action unfolds in Shakespeareâs era, but its heart and head are all about today...As in any jukebox musical, some tunes are wedged in, but others fit surprisingly well...Theatregoers out for a silly good time likely wonât care as they hum along with '& Juliet'."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Its title notwithstanding, '& Juliet' barely takes time to define its heroine; it puts her at the center of the story and then makes her its least interesting character."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "The real stars here are the songs, all from the catalogue of Max Martin and his collaborators...At its best, the show just does away with logic and gives you full-throated renditions of Martinâs more insistent anthems."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Itâs not that '& Juliet' is unenjoyable â it isnât. Somewhere beneath the bombast and repetition and overwrought-from-minute-one approach is a sweet(ish) and smart(ish) tale that gives voice to the marginalized."

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: "What the show lacks in plotting, it more than makes up for musically. It is a jukebox, but itâs a smart one, using the songs in deft, humorous and unexpected ways."

criticReviews.author: Rex Reed
criticReviews.excerpt: " '& Juliet' is quite the most excruciating experience Iâve had on Broadway in decades."

criticReviews.author: Peter Marks
criticReviews.excerpt: "Donât get me wrong: I always crave the deeper communion with a musical that tells a story with songs made new. Like Juliet, though, Iâm happy to bop to a well-produced, familiar beat."

criticReviews.author: Alexis Soloski
criticReviews.excerpt: Criticâs Pick: "Is it electrifying? God, yes. The results are slick, sleek, mordant. Itâs a spine tingler, if not quite the ethics tangler of the original."

criticReviews.author: Kyle Turner
criticReviews.excerpt: "This new adaptation is less about what will happen or how, and without that thrust, Icke's Oedipus struggles to find its meaning."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Ickeâs Oedipus is continuously engaging and smart... but where it runs up against a wall... is in trying to make the story function without gods and fates... I have never seen an Oedipus that truly wrecks."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "Manville and Strong crackle together â their chemistry is steamy and genuine and, in some of the productionâs best moments, after all terrible secrets have been revealed, so is their body-wracking devastation."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "I thought what might follow would be Mr. Ickeâs most provocativeâand logical and interestingâdeparture from Sophocles, an ending of a more ambiguous and less gruesome kind. "

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "Manville, in a blistering and deeply complicated performance, certainly keeps one guessing, until the truth overwhelms her and the audience."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "The ingenuity and precision he delivers with âOedipusâ promise more wild journeys ahead."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "Most of the play takes place in real time in Oedipusâ sleek living room. And Icke puts a pulse-pounding clock onstage that counts down to the election results. But we all know itâs leading up to much more than that."

criticReviews.author: Alexis Soloski
criticReviews.excerpt:
CRITIC'S PICK
"It remains diamond-sharp in its staging and dazzling in its visual imagination, as magical as any spell or potion...Yet there are excisions, most of them so surgical you would never notice, though I did slightly miss the beloved Hogwarts groundskeeper Hagrid...This new version remains ravishingly entertaining, but is also, like the movie adaptations, a more obvious attempt to cash in on Pottermania."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "5/5 stars...Despite its shrinking, 'Harry Potter and the Cursed Child' has kept most of its charm. The spectacular set pieces of John Tiffany’s production remain...The plotting sometimes feels more rushed than before. But the changes have the salutary effect of focusing the story on its most interesting new creations: the resentful Albus Potter (James Romney) and the unpopular Scorpius Malfoy (Brady Dalton Richards), whose bond has been reconceived in a significant way."

criticReviews.author: Zachary Stewart
criticReviews.excerpt: "Some of the actors stumble over their lines as they race through the first half-hour. The sailing is much smoother after that, as the performers are allowed to settle into their characters and inhabit the magical world Tiffany has created with his team of designers...The leaner, meaner version onstage at the Lyric is actually a better play that has lost nothing in terms of production value."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "Every bit as rewarding as the original version. My lack of surprise derives from the theatrical expertise, on every level, evinced by the creators of the two-part version...Potterheads may notice where subplots have been trimmed or eliminated, but the many-tentacled narrative remains virtually the same...And the production retains virtually all of the original’s bedazzlements, from wand battles to levitating Dementors, to quicksilver character transformations."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: "Five hours of performance pass in a wizardly wink of an eye...Everything that happens onstage seems as improbably fluid as, well, time itself. It helps that what happens includes some of the most eye-boggling illusions you’ll ever witness...The new gold standard for fantasy franchise entertainment on Broadway...This slyly manipulative production knows exactly how, and how hard, to push the tenderest spots of most people’s emotional makeups."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "A triumph of theatrical magic...Combines grand storytelling with stagecraft on a scale heretofore unimagined...It is often suspenseful and sometimes downright frightening. Yet amid the cinematic tumult and dazzle of the densely action-packed plot, Thorne and Tiffany carve out quiet scenes of intimacy and tenderness. Great care has gone into creating each moment of this state-of-the-art adventure. It leaves its audience awestruck, spellbound, and deeply satisfied."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "Jam-packed with breakneck plot twists, charming performances, mind-bending spectacle, and, perhaps more surprisingly, moments of theatrical whimsy that feel, amidst the high-tech sorcery, delightfully simple...It effectively weaves serious themes with bouncy adventure narrative, it’s heartfelt and sometimes a touch hokey...You’re pretty much willing to forgive its shortcomings as it sweeps you along in a rush of rip-roaring, good-natured imagination."

criticReviews.author: Terry Teachout
criticReviews.excerpt: "The special effects are sensational, especially if you like theatrical 'black magic'...Plays like a musical—most of the show is underscored and all of the putative song cues are self-evident—and might have been slightly more fun had it been one...To those who have never read a Potter novel or seen a Potter film, 'The Cursed Child' will make no sense at all. Everyone else should find the plot trite, though there’s always something cool to see onstage, which helps a bit."

criticReviews.author: Ben Brantley
criticReviews.excerpt: "The choreography is mostly stuff you could try, accident-free, in your own backyard. And the score consists entirely of songs made famous in the disco era by Abba, music that people seldom admit to having danced to, much less sung in their showers. Yet these elements have been combined, with alchemical magic, into the theatrical equivalent of comfort food."

criticReviews.author: Anita Gates
criticReviews.excerpt: "They’re not dancing in the aisles at Mamma Mia! anymore. Shows do fade. The taverna looks flimsy and cramped on the Broadhurst stage. But its real appeal, beyond those songs, has always been its innate sweetness, and that’s a joy."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "Almost two dozen hits by ABBA form the spine of this worldwide smash, which book writer Catherine Johnson has feebly fleshed out into a mother-daughter comedy-drama. As theater, Mamma Mia! is forgettable. As a delivery system for pop-culture nostalgia, it’s ruthless."

criticReviews.author: John Simon
criticReviews.excerpt: "I found the score neither unbearable nor something I'd miss if I never heard it again...I would not discourage anyone interested from attending Mamma Mia!. But I wouldn't encourage the doubtful, either."

criticReviews.author: Howard Kissel
criticReviews.excerpt: "If you're an ABBA fan, read no further. Just line up at the box office for "Mamma Mia!" Immediately. Since you're already bonded to the material, you will undoubtedly have a wonderful time. If, however, your attachment to ABBA is only tangential or, as in my case, nonexistent, you might want to think twice about it."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "“Mamma Mia!,” which weaves a few threads of romantic comedy around a bumper crop of old Abba tunes, is a thoroughly preposterous show, but it’s also a giddy guilty pleasure...the star of the show is those unnervingly catchy songs, that work happy magic on one’s serotonin levels."

criticReviews.author: Steven Oxman
criticReviews.excerpt: "The musical based on the songs of Abba, is a silly affair all around, and that's its greatest asset. Feather-light, simple, pure pop, set the tone for the evening and provide the lingering sentiment. And feeling is ultimately all that matters with an enjoyably vacuous show like Mamma Mia!"

criticReviews.author: Clive Barnes
criticReviews.excerpt: "Mamma Mia! offers one of those nights when you sit back and let a nutty kind of joy just sweep over you. The score is a nostalgic parade of 22 songs from the alphabetically challenged Swedish pop group of the ’70s. And when you get to the coda finale keep your seats, it ain’t over till it’s over, you’ll be so happy you’ll think you’ve just become a grandparent."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: “ CRITIC’S PICK: 'Stereophonic' is an epic canvas rendered in hyper-intimate detail"

criticReviews.author: Allison Considine
criticReviews.excerpt: "a high-strung, energetic in-studio creation"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "...richly satisfying multitrack production."

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "the play turns into something altogether fresh and, in this play-with-music hybrid form"

criticReviews.author: David Rooney
criticReviews.excerpt: "its searing emotional heft creeps up and grabs you by the throat. It’s a chart topper."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "...it’s easy to get swept up by the terrific original rock songs that throb through it."

criticReviews.author: Dalton Ross
criticReviews.excerpt: "Drama from the studio enters the stage, and it's a hit"

criticReviews.author: David Gordon
criticReviews.excerpt: "the kind of play that reminds you how the magic of theater is a singular experience."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: CRITIC'S PICK: "...it features an eventful story and compelling characters"

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "new musical beautifully juggles circus and theatre"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "The main attraction is the pull of the circus itself."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "...much of 'Water for Elephants' will delight on the basis of spectacle alone"

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "this musical adaptation of the hit novel loses much of its sourceâs pungency and grit."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "Water For Elephants is a pleasant, visually beguiling show"

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a unique and imaginative creation of the stage and live performance."

criticReviews.author: Rex Reed
criticReviews.excerpt: "Everything is so exaggerated and phony that itâs hard to believe"

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a good show and good for the world. "

criticReviews.author: Amelia Merrill
criticReviews.excerpt: "Leigh Silverman’s production is beautiful, but beauty is skin-deep."

criticReviews.author: Regina Robbins
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a full-throated musical call to action, its message is neither subtle nor ambivalent"

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "for all its seriousness, Suffs is full of nerve and spark."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "at times the musical comes across as a bright but exhaustingly busy historical pageant"

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "In 'Suffs,' the message of this thrilling new musical is resoundingly clear"

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "A moving musical march that’s not quite there yet"

criticReviews.author: Rachel Graham
criticReviews.excerpt: "Suffs aims to encourage women to keep going, which is an admirable goal"

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Love is powerful. Dementia is sad. The result can be heartbreaking."

criticReviews.author: Kyle Turner
criticReviews.excerpt: "a trip down memory lane on stage and off"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "As much as I rolled my eyes at The Notebook, I canât deny that they sometimes welled up."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Notebookâs songs at times barely make lyrical sense."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "The musical moves the story forward in time. "

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "...awash in sentimentality and drenched in wistful longings and wish fulfillment."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "...the alterations dull its punch and turn it into a wispy memory play"

criticReviews.author: Emlyn Travis
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Notebook is leaping off the page and onto the stage...its finest adaptation yet."

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: "The final scene, which makes a superb and very cinematic use of a stage turntable, brings us a family that is whole again."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "For all its clairvoyance and foresight about technology, Marjorie Prime’s most potent superpowers are its sensitivity and tenderness."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Marjorie Prime is an interesting artificial-companion piece to Broadway’s other droid show...In Harrison’s script and under Kauffman’s direction, a sense of that evolution creeps up on you."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "Harrison is a formidable craftsman and Marjorie Prime is built very well, but in a way it resembles one of its own artificial humans"

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "People without people’s problems, humor or original insights—which is to say, hardly human at all."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "The play is far more disquieting, merely as a consequence of the passage of time. In fact, I can’t ever remember ever seeing a play whose impact felt so utterly different a decade later."

criticReviews.author: David Cote
criticReviews.excerpt: "True memory is human, imbued with love and grief. The rest is just a simulation."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "Especially impressive is how director Anne Kauffman has taken three of New York’s best-known actors with giant personalities... and made them into one of Broadway’s best and most natural ensembles."

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: "The miracle of this play is that the circle feels as if it is extending to embrace us all."

criticReviews.author: Amelia Merrill
criticReviews.excerpt: "The play hasnât changed â it is still one of the best confrontations with the scope and limits of memory and the memory play itself in recent, well, memory â but its presentation has."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "A searching and revealing drama about the achievements and limits of 1970s feminism, Liberation weaves different kinds of conversation into a multilayered narrativeâand, in doing so, serendipitously restores the very word conversation to its roots."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "The play is constantly running a nail over divisions that seem untraversable, across politics, class, and race, but also across generation and gender, wondering if solidarity could possibly still form there. "

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "Ms. White does elicit uniformly terrific performances that keep the play lively and humming with bright humor."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "Make no mistake, this is a sophisticated piece of writing that goes far beyond the usual 90 minutes on Broadway and is cleverly self-protected too"

criticReviews.author: Aramide Tinubu
criticReviews.excerpt: "Liberation is a brilliant, well-acted, and sobering account of the womenâs rights movement, complicity, and the lens through which we view our caretakers â namely, our mothers."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: " 'Liberation' is timely, but it does more than just appeal to resistance-frazzled audiences."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "The It girl with the spit curl looks great for 100, but her Broadway musical, which feels like one big merch grab, is boop-boop-a-donât"

criticReviews.author: Allison Considine
criticReviews.excerpt: " 'BOOP! The Musical' proves that bringing Betty Boop to life on stage is a worthy endeavor, even if only for the spectacle of it all."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: âThis musical will not change your brain in any way, but it delivers what it promises: a big Broadway production that leaves you grinning, and a star performer with the poise"

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "Unsteadiness in premise can be covered for by verve of execution, which Boop! does find here and there"

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Rogers is a delightful embodiment of Betty, a cartoon that she makes just human enough"

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "She [Rogers] may be playing a two-dimensional character, but sheâs one heâck of a triple threat."

criticReviews.author: Pete Hempstead
criticReviews.excerpt: "With a zippy score, terrific tap numbers...Boop! is one of the feel-good musicals of the year."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: â..such lively, lighthearted funâ¦you might as well sit back and surrender.â

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Queen of Versailles swerves and overcorrects like a drunk driver. Tonally, itâs all over the map...It is the confused, contorted product of a set of absolutely incompatible impulses"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "Rather than eat the rich, the musical settles for nipping them on the nose with all the ferocity of Jackieâs cuddly white Pomeranian."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: A big, splashy effort, slickly professional in nearly every aspect, that has no idea what to make of its heroine. It's a star vehicle with a giant question mark at its center, and its nonjudgmental gaze ultimately leaves one feeling surprisingly neutral.

criticReviews.author: Joseph Pisano
criticReviews.excerpt: It's neither a credible hero's journey nor a compelling antihero's one; it's simply soulless.

criticReviews.author: David Roberts
criticReviews.excerpt: âIn a year when Broadway has given us genuinely ambitious work grappling with what it means to be American, "The Queen of Versailles" offers only spectacle without insight, a palace with no one home. What were they thinking?â

criticReviews.author: Mason Pilevsky
criticReviews.excerpt: The frivolous first act and the stirring second act deliciously dance together.

criticReviews.author: Cary Wong
criticReviews.excerpt: Chenoweth is, of course, the draw, and she tries her hardest to make the material work.

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: Criticâs Pick: "more than an entertaining biomusical with a hummable score. Directed by Michael Arden, itâs also a sociological fairy tale"

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: âThe chance to see two theatrical masterminds go at it for a few hours is sufficient justification for the effort.â

criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "There is love and fandom in every element of this show, like recreations of the movie's outfits and iconic lines"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: âHaving popped its cork early, the show keeps the bubbles flowing freely for the next two hours.â

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: â...hard to dislike and ultimatelyâas a medical examiner might say of these womenâwithout a heartbeat.â

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "Megan Hilty and Jennifer Simard give boisterously funny performances as preening rivals"

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: âThe storyline is cleaner, the characters are clearer, and the pace and the laughs are now non-stop.â

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: âEven if the musical doesnât have a discernible heartbeat, Hilty and Simard ensure Death Becomes Her stays fun and fabulous.â

criticReviews.author: Dalton Ross
criticReviews.excerpt: âItâs a mission that succeeds more often than not.â

criticReviews.author: Elisabeth Vincentelli
criticReviews.excerpt: âThe interconnections between musicians, songs and a society have rarely been evoked as vividly, and as lovingly, as they are in âBuena Vista Social Club.ââ

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "Unapologetically sentimental, the slender story gets the job done."

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "All that adds up to a rousing evening at the theater, if also something less than a great musical."

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: âItâs the most intoxicating and rapturous show of the Broadway season.â

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: âSo transportive are the intoxicating Cuban music and spirited dance that itâs easy to forgive the showâs rather wispy and cliched book.â

criticReviews.author: Zachary Stewart
criticReviews.excerpt: "The music is so good, the performances so alive, and the band so sexy"

criticReviews.author: Mason Pilevsky
criticReviews.excerpt: Concerts disguised as musicals annoy me.

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: "The considerable beauty of this inspiriting show â full of complicated emotions about our diaspora nation â is streaked with melancholy."

criticReviews.author: Joe Dziemianowicz
criticReviews.excerpt: "The simplicity of the production provides breathing room in a megamusical that often exhilarates, but also drains because of its tendency to always think bigger."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "What he delivers in Ragtime is, quite simply, some of the most magnificent singing I have ever heard on Broadway"

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: "The production is so powerfully sung and deeply felt that it overwhelms. Maybe these characters have false dreams, and maybe the showâs idea of hope is impossibly naÃ¯ve, but it lingers."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "This sterling production, with its flawless cast and admirable trenchancy amid an extraordinarily complex plot, augurs well for her tenure."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: â 'Ragtime' is generous to all of its characters...But there is still something touching about its conviction that they will have a better life. I mean, Americans look to musicals for hope, donât we?"

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: "In productions large or small â or, here, imperfectly in-between, though still glorious â everything is the service of the show that creates with words, music and movement a grand American tapestry â tears and all."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "Fortunately, the show sounds gloriously lush throughout...So much so that it hardly needs much embellishment at all."

criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "For those who go to Broadway musicals hoping to hear actors perform songs so powerfully you get goosebumps, youâll find that three times over."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "has plenty of good moves...but no checkmate. Once again, the show blows its assets; shackled to storytelling that is arguably worse than ever, Chess goes down in forfeit."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "But while the singing is always superb, one still wishes that the starsâ barkâand the showâs as a wholeâhad more dramatic bite."

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: "This is the Broadway show of the fall that some will claim to dislike and yet most everyone will enjoy, even if that has to be in secret. "

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: "Although this 'Chess' match may not have produced a new champion, thereâs still some thrilling gameplay, especially from Michele and Christopher, who help provide insight into the magic of 'Chess' "

criticReviews.author: Richard Lawson
criticReviews.excerpt: "In the unending battle between sincerity and snark, Iâm afraid I have to call this particular showdown a draw."

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "If the result is an unwieldy but rousing hot mess with outsize ambitions, maybe now we know how its chess prodigies feel."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "The endless production becomes totally reliant on the amped-up singing of leads... I was board all right."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "Dismayed as I was to endure so much else, I have to admit heâs giving one of Broadwayâs best performances."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Just in Time deals with the difference between image and reality...Itâs finally about the joy of performance, and the escapism it provides not just for an audience but for a performer as well"

criticReviews.author: Caroline Cao
criticReviews.excerpt: "With an exuberant band, Just in Time rides easy on Groffâs waves of showman charisma while paying tribute to the era-specific music and other singers, especially the women in Darinâs life who inspired his performance"

criticReviews.author: Christian Lewis
criticReviews.excerpt: âContrary to its title, âJust in Timeâ is anything but timely, since the window of Darinâs relevancy has long gone.â

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "Itâs another magnificent performance â kind-eyed, honey-voiced and all but irresistible."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: â 'Just in Time' is a wallop of joy, though. And while it doesnât shy away from Darinâs heart struggles, anatomically and romantically, the musical is never gloomy."

criticReviews.author: Kenji Fujishima
criticReviews.excerpt: âNaturally, though, itâs Groffâs energy and charisma that anchor Just in Time.â

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: "...one of the most sensational musical theatre performances I've ever seen."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “The problem is that this version of ‘The Roommate,’ working backward from that fact, delivers a pair of very satisfying performances that cancels out the play.”

criticReviews.author: Amelia Merrill
criticReviews.excerpt: “LuPone knows she can get a laugh from just the quirk of an eyebrow or her delivery of any line, even somber ones. She is engaged with the audience, but not deeply with the character”

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "Sometimes the old can be full of surprises. That’s the running premise of The Roommate, which brings together two very different senior citizens"

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "...Jen Silverman’s funny, moving Broadway play"

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Roommate has Farrow and LuPone to lean into, and their appeal is not small."

criticReviews.author: Daniel D'Addario
criticReviews.excerpt: "Mia Farrow and Patti Lupone bring out each other’s best in a charming double act."

criticReviews.author: Rex Reed
criticReviews.excerpt: "The Roommate, I’m sorry to say, is not very good. Nothing ever happens in it."

criticReviews.author: David Barbour
criticReviews.excerpt: "...a pleasant excuse for stargazing"

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: "...it’s unbearable: in its beauty, yes, but more so in its refusal to offer beauty as a cure when it is only, at best, a comfort."

criticReviews.author: Austin Fimmano
criticReviews.excerpt: "In a way, this production of Our Town is a triumph over that feeling of hopelessness — live theatre returned and continues to thrive — but it also has an important message, asking us to experience every day of our lives to the fullest."

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "But while we in the audience might weep, Wilder's view, though always sympathetic, stays clear and dry. He has an eye on the eternal."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "...with a play like Our Town — where its enduring miracle is both its granular mundanity and its immensity — the imagination is going to start firing."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "Mr. Leon’s 'Our Town' is polished and marked by moments of humor and melancholy"

criticReviews.author: Aramide Tinubu
criticReviews.excerpt: "...it captures the most magnificent part of the human experience—life itself."

criticReviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski
criticReviews.excerpt: "Despite the random contemporary touches, the actors get so mired"

criticReviews.author: Shania Russell
criticReviews.excerpt: "Leon’s inclusive approach to casting means the play better reflects life as we know it."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “...I have to admit that the car alone might be worth a ticket. It fills a deep Broadway longing for large objects performing audience flyovers — and, like the dear departed arthritic chandelier, may be doing so for the foreseeable future.”

criticReviews.author: Gillian Russo
criticReviews.excerpt: “ ‘Back to the Future’ emerges, and continues to be regarded, as a funny, cult-classic romp. The musical adaptation... honors all these views at once and gives ‘Back to the Future’ the larger-than-life presentation it deserves.”

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “What makes ’Back to the Future’ so confusing, aside from the general ineptness, is how little it seems to understand its own relationship to the material it is trying to exploit...A similar fate befalls too many shows that try to cash in on cinematic IP, and the Broadway musical, as an art form, can’t keep getting lost on these roads. If this is the future, please send it back.”

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: “ ‘Back to the Future’ simply tries to hold up its plutonium-weight source material.”

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “The musical has been staged in lavish style...And the DeLorean, with its glowing neon trim, has been glamorized effectively...But the musical as a whole never achieves liftoff, or even the stage equivalent of 88 miles an hour. It cruises along in a low gear for almost three hours.”

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: “With a cast directed to exaggerate every joke, gesture and facial expression – only the always reliable Roger Bart, who plays the eccentric genius inventor Doc Brown, has the chops and instincts to nail the over-the-topness...With a show like ’Back To The Future: The Musical,’ comparisons are, like resistance, futile. And your kids are gonna love it.”

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: “Frenetically paced, relentlessly comedic and visually chaotic, “Back to the Future: The Musical” is aimed squarely at middle America...But the show still misses opportunity after opportunity to make people actually feel.”

criticReviews.author: Frank Rizzo
criticReviews.excerpt: “...with the frequent breaking of the fourth wall and the milking of some meta moments, you wonder what exactly the show’s aiming to be: a self-aware joke for fans or a thrill ride with sincerity.”

criticReviews.author: Laura Collins-Hughes
criticReviews.excerpt: "Gone is the emotional aridity that kept the story at a strange remove."

criticReviews.author: Gillian Russo
criticReviews.excerpt: "Kelli O'Hara and Brian d'Arcy James give career-best performances"

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: "If 'Days and Wine and Roses' isn’t exactly galvanizing...it is effectively sober."

criticReviews.author: Sara Holdren
criticReviews.excerpt: "...the show evokes a specific kind of quietly disheartened sigh."

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: "The show...has a searing power that leaves you both stirred and shaken."

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: "despite its somber theme, Days of Wine and Roses is sumptuous from start to finish"

criticReviews.author: Chris Jones
criticReviews.excerpt: " ‘Days of Wine and Roses,’ a ‘beautifully’ executed musical"

criticReviews.author: Naveen Kumar
criticReviews.excerpt: "There are plenty of joys and sorrows to play even in a straightforward cautionary tale."

criticReviews.author: Jesse Green
criticReviews.excerpt: “Like a lot of current theater that hitches a ride on the Holocaust for dramatic propulsion, ‘Harmony’ makes guilt and anguish its through line, unintentionally suggesting that survival and the solace of music are somehow undeserved. Luckily, after a rough ride of an evening, the finale — offers exquisite evidence to the contrary.”

criticReviews.author: Amelia Merrill
criticReviews.excerpt: “Though its quality is not consistent throughout, ‘Harmony’ has its high points...This immersive quality is chilling, but doesn’t make up for 'Harmony’s' dissonance.”

criticReviews.author: Adam Feldman
criticReviews.excerpt: “The problem with the train story is that, like other plot points, it is underdeveloped: It seems to have been added for extra weight. And that reflects the fundamental problem that Harmony struggles to overcome...As enjoyable and affecting as ‘Harmony’is—and as timely, with antisemitism on the rise worldwide—it doesn’t make the case that, among all that we must never forget, the Comedian Harmonists merit quite this degree of remembrance.”

criticReviews.author: Jackson McHenry
criticReviews.excerpt: “Lines in ‘Harmony’ about the recurrence of hate against Jews and state oppression in general, fashioned as generalities, are suddenly much more charged. The show — basically a fable — doesn’t meet the moment as much as the moment crashes over it.”

criticReviews.author: Charles Isherwood
criticReviews.excerpt: “The superabundance of characters, narratives and context combine to make for the show’s Achilles’ heel. What is unfortunately missing from ‘Harmony’ is a lyrical melding of the varied elements that should be smoothly combined to create a captivating, and harmonizing, whole.”

criticReviews.author: Greg Evans
criticReviews.excerpt: “...’Harmony’ is nonetheless steadily compelling and not infrequently stirring, attributes that speak as much to the Manilow-Sussman craftsmanship as to an intriguing tale long-lost to history.”
